title: field-deploy-lab-iso-factory-notes
content:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic sketch for an ISO/image factory + rack-level bootstrap workflow for field/on-prem cluster deliveries. Target audience: SREs + field ops + infra automation engineers who run site installs and hand off clusters to customers. This is intentionally operational — checklists, failure modes, and terraform notes rather than full-blown design doc.

Scope and goals:
- Support two primary delivery modes: (A) factory ISO built per-customer (airgapped optional) that contains ignition/cloud-init for initial control plane join; (B) PXE/iPXE directed installs for labs and fast swaps.
- Cover bare metal racks and vSphere-managed hosts used as control-plane VMs in constrained environments.
- Provide terraform module notes for idempotent network + DNS + provisioning backend creation.
- Surface upgrade/rollback guardrails for cluster major/minor upgrades in offline/on-prem contexts.

Assumptions:
- Customer provides BMC with IPMI or Redfish reachable from our staging network.
- VLANs and IP ranges are pre-approved and available.
- We can run an image factory VM in our lab that has access to the customer’s image registry or a USB transfer workflow for airgapped sites.

Inventory mapping (example):
- Rack A: 20 compute nodes (mellanox 100G), 2 seed nodes (1U each), 1 vSphere management host (3x NVMe)
- Network: iBGP to leafs, management VLAN 110 (10.1.110.0/24), storage VLAN 120 (10.1.120.0/24)
- BMCs: IP range 10.1.200.0/24, credentials managed in Vault (per-site engine)

High-level workflow (happy path):
1. Preflight: inventory.csv parsed -> terraform apply for management routable network (internal project) -> spawn image factory VM.
2. Build image: packer -> unattended ISO (systemd + ignition) -> inject CSR bootstrap token and kubeadm config with pinned control-plane version.
3. Validation: boot ISO in lab on representative hardware using iPXE test, run conformance smoke tests (kube-system pods, kube-apiserver, etcd quorum, node kubelet ready).
4. Ship/Deploy: transfer ISO to customer (S3 presigned for cloud sites OR USB transfer manifest for airgap). Trigger BMC PXE boot or attach ISO to vSphere VM and power-cycle.
5. Day0 checks: verify node appears in expected k8s cluster, run bootstrap probes, tag nodes in inventory, snapshot logs to central log collector.

Image factory details (notes):
- Base: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS minimal with our kernel/rt patches (if needed).
- Bootstrapping: use systemd-firstboot + Ignition v3 equivalent generated from templates.
- Secrets: do not bake long-lived secrets into ISOs. Use a one-time short-lived bootstrap token (rotate per-ISO). Vault integration: the factory will write ephemeral secrets to an ephemeral GCS/S3 endpoint and then the remote cluster will fetch via one-shot signed URL.
- Airgap: deliver a tarball with OS packages, containerd images, CRI-O images, and a signature file. The ISO should include a small init-script to mount USB and import the tarball.

BMC and provisioning playbook (cheat-sheet):
- Validate BMC credential with ipmitool/redfish cli. Record manufacturer quirks (Dell iDRAC has different overlay for virtual media).
- If BMC unreachable: escalate — manual keyboard/monitor attach, or use iLO local console.
- PXE vs ISO: prefer PXE for repeatability; prefer ISO when network placement or airgap is required.

Terraform module notes (for provisioning infra):
- Module name: redwood/provisioning-site (public naming in repo).
- Inputs to make explicit: management_cidr, bmc_cidr, datacenter, vlan_map (list), allowed_provision_subnets (list), site_id.
- Outputs: image_factory_url, bootstrap_token_id, provisioning_bucket (for airgap).
- Idempotency: make bootstrap_token managed resource with lifecycle replace_on_change = [site_id, image_version]. That way each new ISO triggers a token rotation.
- Secrets: don't store BMC creds in TF state. Use external datasource that fetches creds from Vault at apply-time. Add an apply-time validation step to assert BMC reachability before persist.
- Terraform apply pattern: plan -> apply with -auto-approve only for lab; require PR + manual-confirm for customer applies.

Upgrade plan (offline & online considerations):
- Non-disruptive minor upgrades (patch/minor): prefer in-place kubeadm upgrades on control-plane with one control-plane at a time, drain nodes before kubelet bumps.
- Major version upgrades: perform multi-stage: preflight evals (api deprecations, CRDs), canary control-plane (new VM or pinned control-plane variant), migrate workloads with evictions policy, then cutover.
- Offline sites: pre-build ISO with upgraded control-plane binaries and machine-config that sets MaintenanceMode until operator confirms. Provide a toggle file in /etc/redwood-maint to unblock final steps.
- Rollback: plan includes preserving etcd snapshots before any control-plane upgrade. Snapshot automation: copy to local USB and to offsite (if allowed). Have a tested etcd restore playbook per site.

Health checks and SLO gatekeepers (pre-upgrade):
- API latency < 100ms in lab and site (median 95th).
- etcd leader stable for 5m and commit latency < 50ms.
- CoreDNS p99 < 200ms.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Failed join: common cause is mismatched kubeadm versions or missing CA. Mitigation: capture kubeadm join logs, check token/kubeconfig cluster-CA checksum, reissue ephemeral token.
- BMC virtual media fails on iDRAC: fallback to attach ISO to vSphere management host and boot via VM, then migrate image to physical via dd over network.
- Network segmentation: if provisioning network is misrouted, have a rescue serial console script (socat + nc) to fetch logs remotely.

Quick commands (lab):
- Build image (packer): PACKER_LOG=1 packer build -var-file=site-vars.hcl iso-ubuntu.pkr.hcl
- Start test VM (qemu): qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -m 8G -cdrom out/iso/site.iso -boot d -net nic -net user,hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22
- Generate one-time token (factory): rdwctl token create --site-id S001 --ttl 30m --out token.json

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we best surface hardware SKU quirks into the image factory templates (per-manufacturer kernel cmdline)? Propose a per-site profile registry.
- Should terraform create ephemeral DNS entries for kubeadm SAN entries or rely on static IPs? (current bias: prefer static IPs for airgap determinism).
- Action: Hector to prototype Vault-based one-shot signed URL flow for image secrets (due 2025-10-09).

Hand-off checklist (to solutions / customer success):
- Confirm inventory.csv and node serials are recorded.
- Provide runbook with commands to reissue bootstrap token and restore etcd from supplied snapshot.
- Archive ISO hash and factory build logs in S3 and attach to customer ticket.

References and examples:
- infra-iso-factory repo (internal): github.com/redwood-inference/infra-iso-factory
- Confluence page: Field Deploy Runbook (see linked_artifacts)
- Relevant Jira: JIRA-PLAT-1428 (site id S001 edge deployment)

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally short. We should turn the checklist into an interactive script (rdw-provision) that wraps terraform/packer/qemu steps next quarter.

End of sketch.
